title: A test of text on screen must assert it is visible
rule: When a test proves that a UI part shows some text, assert `toBeVisible()` on that element as well. `toHaveText`, `toHaveCSS` and `boundingBox` all pass on an element under `visibility: hidden`, and a part that waits for a font hides itself exactly that way, so a part that never shows stays green. When the text must be in the family's face, also compare its computed `font-family` with the hero's. Check it by forcing the hiding state on and seeing the test fail. In a Vue mutation use `:class="{ loading: true }"`: a second `class` attribute stops the template compiling, and then every test fails for the wrong reason.
rationale: E42.4 (#455): all 20 tests passed with every reading-test passage forced to `visibility: hidden`, because none asserted that a passage was visible.
